rv.q: But "Gem" is also the least dramatically involving of his plays.

Compared to earlier Wilson plays, which to some extent echo prevalent styles of plays written in their specific decades, Gem of the Ocean may not qualify as “well-made,” but it has dark charm and weaves its own irresistible spell.
Theatregoers will be forever the richer if Wilson, too, never stops asking it.

cn.t: Wilson's spiritually ambitious addition to his century cycle earns praise for its grandly evangelical vision and full-bodied speeches, though the play's miraculous transformations rely on voices and memory rather than spectacle.

vs.sum: The Walter Kerr Theatre offers excellent sightlines and sound quality, making it a great venue for intimate productions. However, the comfort level is below average due to limited legroom and seat width, though the theater's Italian Renaissance-inspired decor adds to its charm.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
